TS-Pico 2.4 is firmware 2.4 with ROM 2.4. **The two go together**: firmware 2.4 needs ROM 2.4, so install both. A board on 2.3 or 2.3.1 needs the new ROM too, and the updaters tick it for you.

**Coming from 1.1?** Read [What's new in the TS-Pico since 1.1](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updates/whats-new-since-1-1/).

## ROM 2.4

- **COPY copies, and MOVE renames.** `COPY "multi.tap" TO "games"` copies a file, and never overwrites one. `MOVE "songs.tap" TO "tunes.tap"` renames a file or moves it to another folder. `MOVE TO "games"` still goes into a folder, `MOVE TO "-"` goes back, and `MOVE TO ""` shows the folder menu. In 2.3, MOVE copied. (#341, #349)
- **FORMAT "name.tap" starts a new, empty tape** and mounts it, ready to SAVE onto. It replaces `tpi:newtap`, which is gone. `FORMAT "tools/"` still makes a folder. (#334, #349)
- **LIST "notes.txt" shows a file**: a text file as text, anything else as a hex dump. `LIST` on its own still lists your program. (#349)
- **RESTORE #4 goes back to the start of a file** open on stream 4, to read it again or write over it, without closing it. (#349)
- **CAT #4 writes a listing into a file** open on stream 4, as plain text: `OPEN #4,"f:files.txt","w": CAT #4: CLOSE #4`. (#404, #406)
- **OPEN #4,"x:" lets a program ask the TS-Pico** which folder it's in, what's mounted, what's in the folder, and the card's label, free space and the versions: `PRINT #4;"path": INPUT #4;p$`. (#404, #405)
- **The card can have a name.** `FORMAT ":GAMES"` labels the card GAMES, the name your computer shows, and `CAT` shows it on the card's line. `FORMAT ":"` takes it off; `SAVE "tpi:label"` shows it. (#349)
- `PRINT PEEK 101` gives **36** (24h), and the start-up line reads `2026 TS-Pico ROM v2.4`.

## Firmware 2.4

- **Bigger folders.** Listings now use far less of the Pico's memory, so a folder of 300 files lists, in color, on a 2.x board. Keep folders to about 100 files for easy reading; 300 have been tested. (#384)
- **SAVE onto the mounted tape**, with append off, now mounts the new file, so `LOAD ""` finds what you just saved. (#362, #365)
- **Colored text brings its own paper**, so a message in blue ink can't vanish on a blue screen. (#370, #374)
- **Messages end their line**, so the next PRINT starts on a new one. (#316, #323)
- **A picture saved with f: is just the picture.** With messages on, `SAVE "f:x.scr" SCREEN$` no longer saves its own "Saving to" line into it. (#314, #322)
- **`tpi:rm` refuses a folder that isn't empty** before it asks, instead of after. (#291)
- **Flash slot 0, the Spectrum ROM, is locked** against `tpi:blkrcv`, so a slip can't overwrite the ROM the update steps rely on. (#294)
- **Cartridges load more reliably.** A 64K `.DCK` goes to the Pico in 32K pieces, and `SAVE "tpi:dock" CODE 2,0` works with a `.DCK` mounted. (#372, #376)
- **`LOAD "tpi:nn"` mounts by number** only with two digits or more, so a file called `7` isn't mistaken for file 007. (#320)
- **The menu** (`LOAD ""` with nothing mounted) has a one-line menu for everyday commands (**T**) and ULA Plus settings for the Pico Video board (**V**). (#340, #363)
- **An auto-mount file**: `SAVE "tpi:automount mymenu.tap"` loads your own menu in place of the built-in one. (#287)
- In Spectrum mode, `SAVE "tpi:dir"` shows every file number on cyan. (#380)
- `OPEN #n,"x:"` "info" gives the SD card's free space. (#415)

## The v3 card

- **The TS2050 modem**, through the card's ESP32 running Zimodem: MTERM and the BASIC dialers work as with a real TS2050, and Hayes mode has flow control. The updaters install Zimodem. (#264–#275, #303–#305, #371)
- **Speech**: the SP0256-AL2 from its ROM. `SAVE "tpi:say HELLO"`, `OPEN #4,"v:"` to speak what you print, ports 17 and 37 for programs written for a speech board, and a greeting at switch-on (`tpi:greet`). (#282, #286, #289, #375, #377)
- **Tapes over WiFi**: `tpi:wifi` joins your network and `tpi:net` finds and downloads 2068 tapes from the TS-Pico collection on archive.org, every one tested to load. A tape over 48K goes into the card's PSRAM. (#385, #408, #412)
- **A Kempston joystick** on the DE-9 socket, at port 31. (#364)
- **The 8 MB PSRAM** is in use: 1 MB more memory for the firmware. (#410, #411, #413)
- **The SD socket is switched off** between mounts. (#262, #407)
- ROM and cartridge slots can boot straight from the SD card. (#263)

## Manuals

- **A Quick Start Guide**, eight pages, and **a Quick Reference Guide**, a letter sheet folded in three in the style of the one that came with the 2068. (#353)
- The user manual leads with the BASIC keywords and uses `tpi:` only where there's none, with new drawings of the 2068 and the board. (#343, #367, #369)
- The programmer's manual has a reference part (picolib and the BIOS) and Appendix F, writing channel code for the TS-2068. (#326, #329)

## For programmers

- **Byte 2 of a command pre-header is 24h** on ROM 2.4. Send the same from your own code; `picolib.asm` does.
- The `x:` channel and `CAT #` give a program the folder and the card without parsing the screen. See the user manual, chapter 6 (6.9 for `x:`) and CAT in chapter 10.
- The [programmer's manual](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/manual/programmers-manual.html) and the [programmer's reference](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/docs/) describe 2.4.

## Installing

1. **Switch the TS-2068 off.**
2. Open the [web updater](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updater/) in Chrome or Edge, connect the TS-Pico by USB, choose **Latest release**, and follow the steps. On Windows, run **TS-Pico-Updater.exe** from this release instead.
3. On a 2.x board, the updater ticks **Update the TS-2068 ROM** for every board not already on 2.4, 2.3 boards included. Leave it ticked: without ROM 2.4, firmware 2.4 doesn't work properly. The ROM update erases the Pico's own files first and puts fresh ones back, so settings you changed in `config.ini` go back to their defaults. The SD card is not touched.
4. Keep the **P10 jumper** fitted.

Afterwards, `SAVE "tpi:info"` shows firmware 2.4 and ROM 2.4. `PRINT PEEK 101` gives **36** (ROM 2.4).

The v3 card needs no ROM step: its ROMs are slot files, which the updaters copy with the firmware.

## Downloads

- `firmware.uf2`: the TS-Pico 2.x firmware, for dragging onto the Pico's RPI-RP2 drive by hand.
- `firmware-v3.uf2`: the v3 card's firmware, for its RP2350 drive.
- `v3-slots.zip`: the v3 card's ROM and cartridge slot files, for `/slots`.
- `upgrade.uf2`: the ROM updater (2.x boards).
- `TS-Pico-Updater.exe`: the updater for Windows (2.x boards and the v3 card).
- `Pico-v2.4.rom`: the whole 512K flash image (2.x boards).
- `user-manual-half-letter.pdf`, `user-manual-saddle-stitch-letter.pdf`: the user manual.
- `pico_host-*.zip`: the TS-Pico firmware for emulators, for macOS, Linux and Windows. Use it with ROM 2.4. See the emulator guide.
- The release zip: the firmware, the Pico's files, ROM 2.4 (`src/rom/TSPICO-24.ROM`) and the SD card files.
